Axiom: A ticket closes on its own phase gates — `[x] DONE` is mechanical close, not verification. Audit (and, on the same trigger, code-review) target the GROUP, not the lone ticket: every ticket of one spec, reviewed together once the group's LAST ticket closes — a review torn out of its spec loses the cross-ticket context it needs. `sdd-execute` asks the tool for the moment, never eyeballs it: `sdd-task --audit-group ` returns `due` once every ticket in the group is `[x] DONE`, or `not yet` naming what remains open. `not yet` → dispatch NEITHER audit nor code-review this cycle; proceed to the next ticket in the queue — a ticket's own dependents INSIDE the same group unblock on ITS closure alone, same as always. `due` → dispatch the group audit, then, once it passes, the group code-review. Until the group's audit returns PASS, TICKETS OF OTHER SPECS that depend on this spec stay blocked; tickets inside this group are never held by it.
